newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australis has US$95 mln equity pledged.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australis has US$95 mln equity pledged.

text.p: Pay television operator Australis Media Ltd said it secured extra equity commitments of US$15 million, which together with a previously reported $80 million, will inject $95 million on new cash equity into the company.
Australis said it had received written indication from its bondholders to allow the recapitalisation of the company to proceed.
The company said it remains in negotiations to secure a further equity commitment of a minimum of US$5 million by shareholders, which would bring new equity to US$100 million.
It said the indicated support from most of its bondholders to the recapitalisation plan was conditional upon raising at least US$100 million in new equity, among other things.

Lenfest Communications Inc of the United States had agreed to convert its technical services agreement into ordinary stock or convertible notes and Lenfest's loan of US$18.5 million has been extended until October 31 this year, Australis said.
Australis said most bondholders had indicated their consent to the raising of a further US$150 million in senior debt.

Their consent was subject to changes in their own agreements including an annual interest payment of at least 14 percent, a cash payment to existing bondholders, a lower warrant exercise price, and Australis finding US$100 million of new equity.
Australis has been locked in talks in the last two months to secure a new debt package that would allow it to continue trading in the medium term.
The talks stalled on issues such as the new debt's ranking and the role of shareholders in raising more equity.

Shareholders include Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd, the AMP Society, Guiness Peat Group Plc, United International Holdings Inc, and Lenfest, which is an affiliate of cable group Telecommunications Inc.
Australis said on August 20 that its shareholders would provide US$105 million of equity, with Lenfest to contribute US$65 million and Packer US$15 million.
It said on Friday the agreement indicated from bondholders included approval of the plan to share infrastructure with rival pay tv group Optus Vision. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
